initialPrompts.observatory:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one original premium hand-painted 2.5D portrait mobile puzzle-game environment for Starfall, an inhabited miniature world with sculpted storybook forms, generous rounded bevels, simplified tactile material, dramatic local contact shadows. This is a total reimagining of our environment, not a scenic wallpaper. CLOSE overhead tabletop/diorama view; no distant horizon. The entire image is the game scene, no phone frame or presentation border. Portrait ratio 393:852.
COMPOSITION CONTRACT: the uninterrupted playable surface runs from x=5.8% to94.2%, y=26% to70.5%, with nearly parallel edges and very shallow overhead perspective; all 49 future game cells fit there. Keep this entire central rectangular area quiet, dark desaturated material with very low-frequency shading. No visible grid, paths, seams across the middle, engraved star map, game pieces or decorative stars inside it. A few LARGE sculpted scenic masses live above y=18% and below y=73%, with thin organic edges along the sides. The surrounding world must physically form the playing surface. It is not a generic ornate rectangular frame. Avoid a huge blank scenic top half; objects must be close and large.
UI ARCHITECTURE: reserve three small dark native-content recesses at y=19-24%: score on the left, a shallow forecast channel in the middle, and a menu socket on the right, built into this world's actual material. At y=77-91% reserve an uninterrupted dark text-reading surface from x=10-74%, physically part of a lower ledge or desk, sharing the same architecture, shading and contact. Below it, y=92-96%, allow two native action positions; no painted buttons or text. The right bottom corner can host one large secondary prop. Keep comfortable breathing room. Whole scene visible with grounded joints, no floating cutouts.
STYLE: inviting, intimate, high-end fantasy game illustration. Broad intentional shapes and brushwork, expressive silhouettes, restrained ornament, readable at phone scale. Rich edge materials, quiet center. The stars will be added separately using existing game assets. Do not paint stars, jewels, faces, writing, numbers, logos or UI icons. No copied Blizzard assets or franchise symbols. No photorealism, flat vector art, giant marble slab, shiny gold piping everywhere, symmetrical generic frame, or distant vistas.
WORLD: MOONLIT OBSERVATORY — a close astronomer's worksite cut into a small rounded midnight-blue lunar rock. The playable area is a deep matte indigo astronomical collecting well, broad and calm, with a few uneven moonstone edges that open naturally onto the worksite. Upper left: one substantial brushed-brass telescope with a clear pivot and thick stone pedestal joined to the surrounding architecture, lens pointing up and away from the playfield. Upper right: a small copper-roof dome with a warm slit window, built into the same rock. They occupy the upper corners, not the playing rectangle. The top score/forecast/menu recesses are small brass instrument insets in a low stone sill. Lower edge: a thick worn wooden astronomer's desk partly inset into the rock, dark plum writing surface for the dialogue, large readable forms. Lower right: a single warm lantern anchored by its base on the desk, adjacent short brass cable running through the desk edge. A few quiet crystal flowers only at the extreme edge. Warm amber localized light, cool dusty periwinkle rock, dark inky central floor. Surrounding negative space is a soft close cosmic haze, no giant galaxy vista. Make it feel like somewhere a tiny astronomer works, solid and welcoming.

WORLD: PRISM TIDE GROTTO — a continuous thick, translucent sea-glass tidal vessel cradled in a few smooth coral-stone outcrops. It must feel materially unlike a stone terrace: rounded blue-green glass cross-sections, subtle violet refraction on a few thick rim edges, dark transparent depth, soft cool local light. The central playing surface is an almost-black petrol-blue calm pool/frosted glass floor with very low contrast. No bright watery caustics under pieces. Upper left: a sculpted spiral shell fountain grounded into a pale coral rock, a single fine stream contained in a narrow side gutter outside the playing area. Upper right: thick mineral-glass lip curves around a small quiet rock and sea grass. The small score/forecast/menu recesses are frosted dark glass hollows in the back lip, with no metal/gold trim. Bottom: the same continuous thick glass curves outward into a dark frosted reading shelf, text area remains flat and quiet. Lower right: one substantial open shell on an attached stone seat containing a soft luminous pearl, visibly attached to the glass vessel base. Calm surrounding shallow water fills the corners; pale coral, small sea grass and restrained water glints at the perimeter. No temple columns, no palace, no rectangular metallic frame. Intimate close top-down little tidal world.

WORLD: CLOUDSEA CONSERVATORY — a small suspended botanical greenhouse nursery, warmly handcrafted. The play surface is a broad dark desaturated blue-sage velvet moss bed/nursery tray, extremely quiet and flat, held by softly curved weathered rosewood roots and matte ivory ceramic. Unlike a stone board: warm fibrous wood, swollen ceramic corners, hanging braided supports and living growth at the edges. Upper left: a tall elegant wooden wind harp rooted in the nursery rail, with a few large clear strings and leaves curling around its feet. Upper right: one miniature sage-and-copper glasshouse with misted rounded glass panes and a glowing dew vessel. Large toy-like forms. A few oversized leaves and one trailing vine, no dense forest. Top native score/forecast/menu hollows are carved into a low rosewood nursery rail, muted dark interiors. Lower edge: a potting bench growing naturally out of the same wooden framework with a quiet dark green soft mat for dialogue. Lower right: an ivory ceramic dew catcher with a broad leaf-shaped funnel, large single clear drop and a small connected collection bowl. One folded cloth and a small terracotta pot as secondary texture, uncluttered. Warm peach diffuse dawn outside in soft cream clouds that stay at the extreme perimeter. No distant landscape, massive columns, stone slab, golden jewel frame or ornamental metal flourishes. A breathable nurturing miniature garden high above the clouds.

rejectedGuideCorrection:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the environment painting to correct. Image 2 is a TECHNICAL LAYOUT GUIDE ONLY. Preserve the world, material rendering, lighting and large scenic objects of Image 1. Correct just the physical space available to play.
The full dark rectangle in guide 2 (x4.2–95.8%, y24.5–72%) must become uninterrupted quiet dark play material in image 1. All four corners must be usable, square-ish with only tiny corner rounding OUTSIDE that rectangle. Move/reshape the surrounding rims and all props OUTSIDE it. Move the upper control rail and upper scenery up so the rail finishes ABOVE y24.5%. Move the lower scenic edge, desk and foreground props DOWN so none enter above y72%. Thin the side rims to the outermost 4% of image width through this entire area. Do not merely paint a flat rectangle over the art: rebuild its physical joins, perspective and shadows convincingly. Preserve the same close rich miniature scene around it. The lower reading desk and action wells can be shifted a little lower to accommodate the correction but keep them usable and physically joined.
No stars, character faces, labels, pink border, grid, numbers, guide text or geometry lines in the output. The guide is not artwork and must disappear entirely. Keep dark play material subtly textured like the original. Maintain the original portrait aspect ratio and overall scene appearance. This is production layout correction, not a redesign into a different world.
selectedCorrection:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Make a small spatial correction to this existing portrait game-board painting. Preserve the entire overall composition, all three TOP CONTROL RECESSES, both BOTTOM ACTION RECESSES, reading mat, material rendering and every major object. All five control recesses must stay fully visible inside the canvas. Do not remove them or crop them. Do not greatly enlarge or lengthen the center.
Correct the playable rectangle: move the TOP control sill upward just a little, so its bottom is at 24% of the full image height. The calm playing floor immediately below it should have straight-ish edges from x=4% to x=96%, down to y=72%. At its bottom, move the foreground rim down just enough to follow y=72%, with small corners OUTSIDE that rectangle. Push any intruding flowers, leaves, tools or scenic props into the outermost 4% side margins or BELOW y=72%. No large prop may cross into the playing rectangle.
Keep the lower reading shelf fully visible from y=77% to89%, including its material and mounted prop. Scale the lower-right prop down slightly if needed so it can sit below y=72% while retaining its visible solid base. Place the TWO bottom action recesses together at y=91% to96%, FULLY visible with a small margin below. Keep their openings broad and practical, not tiny circles. The last 3% is foreground edge.
This is a modest correction to the original artwork, not a new layout. Retain its richness and style. Add no characters, game pieces, writing or UI content. Keep exactly the same portrait aspect.
